:::{#thm-continuous-several}
#### Continuity in one variable, and sums, multiples and compositions

1. For $p = q = 1$, a function $f$ is continuous at $x$ in the sense of @def-continuous-several
   exactly when $\lim_{y \to x} f(y) = f(x)$ ([limit](calculus.qmd#def-limit)),
   which is the usual [continuity](calculus.qmd#def-continuous) at $x$.
2. If $f : \reals^p \to \reals^q$ is continuous at $\vx$ and $g : \reals^q \to \reals^r$ is continuous at $f(\vx)$,
   then the [composition](sets-functions.qmd#def-composition) $g \circ f$ is continuous at $\vx$.
3. If $f, g : \reals^p \to \reals$ are continuous at $\vx$, then $f + g$ is continuous at $\vx$.
4. If $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ is continuous at $\vx$ and $c \in \reals$, then $c f$ is continuous at $\vx$.

If the hypotheses of part 2, 3 or 4 hold at every point of a set,
the conclusion holds at every point of that set.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

Let $\tolout > 0$ be given.

**Part 1.**
For $p = q = 1$, $\norm{f(y) - f(x)} = \abs{f(y) - f(x)}$ and $\norm{y - x} = \abs{y - x}$.
@def-continuous-several then asks for a $\tolin > 0$ such that
$\abs{f(y) - f(x)} < \tolout$ whenever $\abs{y - x} < \tolin$.
The [limit definition](calculus.qmd#def-limit) with $L = f(x)$ asks for the same inequality, but only whenever $0 < \abs{y - x} < \tolin$.
The two agree, because at $y = x$ the inequality $\abs{f(x) - f(x)} = 0 < \tolout$ holds for every $\tolin$.

**Part 2.**
Because $g$ is continuous at $f(\vx)$, there is a $\tolin_g > 0$ such that
$\norm{g(\vecf{z}) - g(f(\vx))} < \tolout$ whenever $\norm{\vecf{z} - f(\vx)} < \tolin_g$.
Because $f$ is continuous at $\vx$, applied with $\tolin_g$ in the role of $\tolout$,
there is a $\tolin > 0$ such that $\norm{f(\vy) - f(\vx)} < \tolin_g$ whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \tolin$.
So if $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \tolin$, then $\vecf{z} = f(\vy)$ has $\norm{\vecf{z} - f(\vx)} < \tolin_g$,
and therefore $\norm{g(f(\vy)) - g(f(\vx))} < \tolout$.

**Part 3.**
Because $f$ and $g$ are continuous at $\vx$, there are $\tolin_f > 0$ and $\tolin_g > 0$ such that
$\abs{f(\vy) - f(\vx)} < \tolout / 2$ whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \tolin_f$,
and $\abs{g(\vy) - g(\vx)} < \tolout / 2$ whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \tolin_g$.
Let $\tolin \eqdef \min\cb{\tolin_f, \tolin_g}$.
If $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \tolin$, then

$$
\ba
\abs{(f + g)(\vy) - (f + g)(\vx)}
&= \abs{\paren{f(\vy) - f(\vx)} + \paren{g(\vy) - g(\vx)}}
&& \text{(regroup)}
\\
&\le \abs{f(\vy) - f(\vx)} + \abs{g(\vy) - g(\vx)}
&& \text{(triangle inequality for numbers)}
\\
&< \frac{\tolout}{2} + \frac{\tolout}{2}
&& \text{(choice of } \tolin \text{)}
\\
&= \tolout.
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

**Part 4.**
Because $f$ is continuous at $\vx$, there is a $\tolin > 0$ such that
$\abs{f(\vy) - f(\vx)} < \tolout / (\abs{c} + 1)$ whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \tolin$.
For such $\vy$,

$$
\ba
\abs{c f(\vy) - c f(\vx)}
&= \abs{c}\,\abs{f(\vy) - f(\vx)}
&& \text{(factor out } c \text{)}
\\
&\le \abs{c}\,\frac{\tolout}{\abs{c} + 1}
&& \text{(choice of } \tolin \text{)}
\\
&< \tolout.
&& \text{(} \abs{c} < \abs{c} + 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
